source_text: Sed de sacrificiis et sacerdotiis quid loquar? de spectaculis autem et uoluptatibus eiusmodi suum iam uolumen impleuimus. hoc loco retractari oportet de festis diebus et aliis extraordinariis sollemnitatibus, quas interdum lasciuiae, interdum timiditati nostrae subscribimus aduersus fidem disciplinamque communicantes nationibus in idolicis rebus. de hoc quidem primo consistam, an cum ipsis quoque nationibus communicare in huiusmodi seruus dei debeat siue habitu siue uictu uel quo alio genere laetitiae earum. gaudere cum gaudentibus et lugere cum lugentibus de fratribus dictum est ab apostolo ad unanimitatem cohortante. ceterum ad haec nihil communionis est lumini et tenebris, uitae et morti, aut scindimus quod est scriptum: saeculum gaudebit, uos uero lugebitis. si cum saeculo gaudemus, uerendum est, ne cum saeculo et lugeamus. saeculo autem gaudente lugeamus et saeculo postea lugente gaudebimus. sic et Eleazar apud inferos in sinu Abrahae refrigerium consecutus, contra diues in tormento ignis constitutus alternas malorum et bonorum uices aemula retributione compensant. sunt quidam dies munerum, quae apud alios honoris titulum, apud alios mercedis debitum expungunt. nunc ergo, inquis, recipiam meum uel rependam alienum. si hunc morem sibi homines de superstitione consecrauerunt, tu extraneus ab omni eorum uanitate quid participas idolothyta sollemnia, quasi tibi quoque praescriptum sit de die, quominus id, quod homini debes uel tibi ab homine debetur, citra diei obseruationem luas uel recipias. da formam, in qua uelis agi tecum. cur enim et lateas, cum ignorantia alterius tuam conscientiam contamines? si non ignoraris quod sis Christianus, temptaris et contra conscientiam alterius agis tamquam non Christianus: sin uero et dissimulaueris, temptatus addictus es. certe siue hac siue iliac, reus es confusionis in deo. qui autem confusus super me fuerit penes homines, et ego confundar super illo, inquit, penes patrem meum, qui est in caelis.
thought_title: Christians must not share pagan festive days
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that a servant of God must not join pagans in their festive days and celebrations, because these are idolatrous.
pass_a_gloss: But what shall I say about sacrifices and priesthoods? About spectacles and pleasures of that kind we have already filled our own volume. At this point it is necessary to treat again of festive days and other extraordinary solemnities, which we sometimes subscribe to our wantonness, sometimes to our timidity, against faith and discipline, sharing with the nations in idolatrous matters. On this point indeed I will first take my stand, whether a servant of God ought to share with the nations themselves in things of this kind, either in dress or in food or in any other kind of their rejoicing. To rejoice with those who rejoice and to mourn with those who mourn was said by the apostle about brothers, urging to unanimity. But for the rest, for these things there is no communion between light and darkness, between life and death, or we split what is written: the world will rejoice, but you will mourn. If we rejoice with the world, it is to be feared that we may also mourn with the world. But while the world rejoices, let us mourn, and when the world later mourns, we will rejoice. So also Eleazar in the underworld obtained refreshment in Abraham's bosom, while the rich man, placed in the torment of fire, they compensate the alternating turns of evils and goods with rival retribution. There are certain days of gifts, which among some discharge the title of honor, among others the debt of payment. Now then, you say, I will receive my own or repay another's. If men have consecrated this custom to themselves from superstition, you, a stranger to all their vanity, why do you share in solemnities of things offered to idols, as if it were also prescribed to you about the day, that you may not pay or receive what you owe to a man or is owed to you by a man without observance of the day. Give a form in which you wish to be dealt with. For why do you also hide, when by the ignorance of another you contaminate your own conscience? If you are not known to be a Christian, you are tempted and you act against the conscience of another as if not a Christian: but if you have also concealed it, tempted you are condemned. Certainly whether in this way or in that, you are guilty of confusion in God. But whoever has been ashamed of me before men, I also will be ashamed of him, he says, before my Father, who is in heaven.

lemmas.gloss: you are tempted, you are tested

choices.english: solemnities of things offered to idols
choices.why: The glossary requires 'things offered to idols' for idolothyta; 'solemnities' preserves the festive-observance sense of sollemnia.
Saeculum here means the present age or world opposed to God, matching the quoted saying about the world rejoicing.
The glossary uses 'pagans' for ethnici, but here the source has nationibus; 'nations' keeps the literal term while the context makes clear they are pagan nations.
Confusio here means shame or disgrace; 'confusion in God' preserves the literal phrase and the following quotation about being ashamed of Christ.
Aemula means rival or competing; the phrase describes the matching recompense of good and evil in the afterlife.

pass_b_english: But why should I speak of sacrifices and priesthoods? I have already filled a volume on spectacles and pleasures of that kind. At this point I must return to the question of feast days and other extraordinary solemnities, which we sometimes subscribe to out of self-indulgence, sometimes out of timidity, sharing with the pagans in idolatrous matters against faith and discipline.

On this point I will first settle whether a servant of God ought to share with the pagans themselves in such things, whether in dress or in food or in any other kind of their rejoicing. "Rejoice with those who rejoice and mourn with those who mourn" was said by the apostle about brothers, urging unity of mind (Romans 12:15). But for these things there is no fellowship between light and darkness, life and death, or we tear apart what is written: "The world will rejoice, but you will mourn" (John 16:20). If we rejoice with the world, we must fear that we will also mourn with the world. But while the world rejoices, let us mourn, and when the world later mourns, we will rejoice.

So also Eleazar in the underworld received refreshment in Abraham's bosom, while the rich man was placed in the torment of fire, and they repay the alternating turns of evils and goods with rival retribution (Luke 16:23-25).

There are certain days of gifts, which among some discharge a title of honor, among others a debt of payment. "Now then," you say, "I will receive what is mine or repay what belongs to another." If people have consecrated this custom to themselves out of superstition, why do you, a stranger to all their vanity, participate in solemnities of things offered to idols, as though a day had been prescribed for you too, so that you cannot pay what you owe to a person or receive what is owed to you by a person without observing the day? Set your own terms for how you wish to be treated.

For why do you hide, when by another's ignorance you contaminate your own conscience? If you are not known to be a Christian, you are tempted and you act against another's conscience as though you were not a Christian; but if you have concealed it, you have been tempted and condemned. Certainly, whether this way or that, you are guilty of confusion in God. "Whoever is ashamed of me before men, I will also be ashamed of him," he says, "before my Father who is in heaven" (Matthew 10:33).
